title: Lean target for a homologically twisted Kirby four-manifold invariant, revision 2
top_notice: This is a formalization objective and obligation ledger, not a theorem claim. The explicit three-handle normalization and the generic chain-derived marked-H2 transport mechanism are established. No concrete four-manifold invariant has yet been constructed because three hard conditions remain open.

objective.goal: Construct admissible FourManifoldInvariantInputs from concrete category, evaluator, Kirby-presentation, and marked-homology data, then prove that the normalized value is independent of the certified special Kirby presentation.
objective.target_statement: For any marked closed oriented four-manifold pair and any two certified special Kirby realizations of that same marked pair, the two normalized evaluator values are equal.
objective.acceptance_rule: The target is established only after one concrete, source-backed construction supplies all six required conditions. Merely postulating or arbitrarily inhabiting the nested Lean structures is not admissible evidence.

established.scope: Abstract algebraic interface and previously formalized local graphical consequences only.
established.caveat: The concrete evaluator compiler that instantiates this interface for actual category data remains open.

established.scope: The normalization contribution of a three-handle and its cancellation with the isolated two-handle factor are explicit Lean theorems.
established.notation_warning: If the total quantum dimension is written as script-D with script-D^2 = d(C), then the three-handle weight is script-D^-2, not script-D^-1.

established.scope: A presentation carries an integral handle chain complex. Every admitted move supplies a chain homotopy equivalence, and Lean derives the additive equivalence on second homology and the inverse-precomposition character transport.
silent_failure_guards: MarkedH2Transport has no handwritten homologyEquiv field.
MarkedH2Transport has no handwritten targetCharacter field.
The ambient H2 coordinate model must be an AddCommGroup and the coordinate identification must be an AddEquiv.
established.remaining_boundary: Binding each concrete Kirby diagram and move to its actual handle boundary matrices, bases, and chain equivalence remains part of concrete_marked_pair_assembly.

open.required_result: Compile concrete category and coupon/link syntax into the abstract prescription and prove every local-step equation used by the presentation-independence theorem.
open.failure_guard: An arbitrary inhabitant of the prescription structure is rejected as evidence.

open.required_result: Bind an exact source-backed theorem showing that any two allowed special presentations of the same closed oriented four-manifold are connected by the represented move system.
open.failure_guard: A finite list of verified local moves is not by itself accepted as a completeness theorem.

open.required_result: Bind concrete diagrams to handle chain matrices and move chain maps, prove marked-coordinate compatibility, and assemble the evaluator and complete presentation system into one admissible target input.
open.failure_guard: The generic H2 mechanism is not misreported as concrete diagram certification, and the target theorem is not promoted while the concrete input instance is absent.

h2_specific_rejections: A handwritten H2 equivalence is not a field of MarkedH2Transport.
A handwritten transported character is not a field of MarkedH2Transport.

explicit_non_claims: This note does not claim that a four-manifold invariant has been established.
This note does not claim special Kirby calculus completeness from the currently encoded local moves.
This note establishes the generic chain-derived H2 mechanism but does not certify concrete diagram boundary matrices or move chain maps.
This note does not claim that the abstract evaluator interfaces have been instantiated by a concrete category and link/coupon compiler.
This note does not identify the construction with the Crane-Yetter or Yetter state-sum invariant.
This note does not claim a theorem merely from the existence of abstract Lean structures with semantic proof fields.
